status: Private original campaign briefs; sources below are exclusion inventory IDs only, never runtime dependencies

briefs.title: The Quiet Nursery
briefs.story: A nursery habitat's root cultures are failing even though its environmental reports show perfect conditions. The reports average away short pressure pulses caused by a shared ventilation controller. The commander measures the pulses, carries a reference culture to a test berth and helps the growers choose independent breathing cells or a jointly supervised controller.
survey: Measure three pressure pulses outside the nursery's service vents.
KEST: Averages hide the moment when a root stops breathing. Record the shortest pulse as carefully as the longest.
work: Install the reference culture in the isolated orbital test cradle.
VEIL: The reference belongs to the growers. Keep its containment sealed until the receiving cradle acknowledges the same serial capsule.
mission_action_confirmed
second: Escort the consenting horticulture tender to the test berth.
VEIL: The gardeners will inspect their own crop. An empty tender or a flight recorder cannot stand in for their arrival.
escort_arrived
choices: Give each nursery cell an independent air regulator
Verify the two independent regulator locks and their separate pressure tests.
KEST: Isolation must work under a pulse, not merely appear as a switch label.
Establish a shared grower-controlled ventilation schedule
Verify the grower countersignature and the bounded ventilation schedule.
VEIL: Shared air requires a published limit and a way for every cell to stop the controller.
clue: The breath between readings
The unaveraged pressure trace includes a quiet inward curl that no nursery valve produces.
briefs.cover: an orbital botanical laboratory with a pale jade sealed root-culture capsule, three delicate pressure traces and translucent growing cells beyond a window; patient horticultural science, no animals or infestation

briefs.title: Borrowed Dawn
briefs.story: Three orbital homes depend on a leased sunlight reflector whose ownership contract has expired. Its automatic parking motion will leave one habitat cold while overheating another. The commander measures the actual illumination, moves a work crew through a safe corridor and establishes either independent mirror limits or a public light-sharing schedule.
survey: Scan the three illumination monitors before the reflector moves.
RELL: The sun is not failing. Our agreement about where the light goes has failed.
work: Lock two reflector actuators inside their measured safe travel envelopes.
PENN: These are external actuator collars. Touching them does not breach or damage a station.
mission_action_confirmed
second: Escort the identified mirror crew to the shadow-side service berth.
PENN: Keep the tender in the clear corridor. We need the actual crew to test the locks.
escort_arrived
choices: Give each habitat its own bounded reflector segment
Test independent segment stops and receive both habitat approvals.
RELL: One controller must not be able to steal another home's dawn.
Publish a joint illumination rota
Verify the signed rota and its physical over-temperature cutoff.
PENN: A timetable is useful only if the machinery obeys its limit.
clue: The unlit interval
A photometer records a curved shadow during an interval when no physical reflector crosses its view.
briefs.cover: a dark orbital solar-control alcove, three gold light paths from separated mirror segments above a cool blue planet; a bronze illumination meter and manual actuator collar in foreground, no exploding star

briefs.title: The Open Shadow
briefs.story: A civilian rescue service uses a privacy filter that hides passenger identities but should never hide collision warnings. An update has coupled the two channels. The commander compares cooperative test vessels, installs an independently measured reference and negotiates either public collision telemetry or a witnessed privacy escrow.
survey: Compare identity and collision channels on three consenting calibration beacons.
VALE: Privacy is a right. Silence on a collision channel is a physical hazard. Measure them separately.
work: Attach the reference receiver to two external test couplers.
RENN: The reference listens without recording a passenger's identity. Keep the two receipts distinct.
mission_action_confirmed
second: Guide the volunteer test tender through the measured crossing corridor.
VALE: Its pilot knows the test. Do not use an uninformed traveller as bait.
escort_arrived
choices: Publish anonymous collision telemetry
Verify the anonymous broadcast and independent close-pass warning.
VALE: Publish movement, not names.
Use a witnessed identity escrow with a safety channel
Verify the escrow witness and continuously open collision channel.
RENN: Closing the archive must never close the warning.
clue: The shadow with no hull
The passive comparison contains an inward-moving phase shadow without an associated vessel or identity record.
briefs.cover: an empty orbital sensor-testing chamber, a circular passive receiver comparing a steady cyan collision trace with a veiled amber identity trace, dark glass and restrained teal light

briefs.title: Harbour Without Orders
briefs.story: A port's arrival allocator has lost its signing authority after a disputed maintenance transfer. No one is attacking the station, but every berth refuses every arriving ship. The commander establishes who can authorise safe approaches, brings in an independent traffic witness and tests either distributed berth authority or a temporary public harbour office.
survey: Scan the three external arrival allocators and record their refusal certificates.
RELL: The harbour is intact. Its doors are closed by three mutually invalid signatures.
work: Install temporary safety limits at the two external approach relays.
VOSS: These limits prevent conflicting approaches while the operators decide who may sign.
mission_action_confirmed
second: Escort the neutral traffic witness to the emergency receiving berth.
RELL: Reception must identify our witness and the berth used. A ship disappearing near the station proves nothing.
escort_arrived
choices: Return authority to independent berth operators
Verify two operator keys and a conflict-free simultaneous approach test.
VOSS: Each berth may sign its own approach, within the common exclusion envelope.
Create a time-limited public harbour office
Verify the public key register and its automatic authority expiry.
RELL: Emergency authority must come with a visible end.
clue: The unsigned berth
The allocator's oldest signed audit describes an empty central berth enclosed by a curved approach boundary.
briefs.cover: a civilian orbital harbour-control room, three closed cyan arrival tracks around an empty docking coordinate, an amber authority module on a workbench, no battle or occupied station

briefs.title: False Colours
briefs.story: A lawful hauler is being mistaken for a patrol vessel because a transponder recycler issued duplicate identity keys. A frightened militia has closed the freight corridor. The commander obtains the original key chain, protects a cooperative verification flight and chooses public revocation or a supervised reissue. Attributed evidence resolves the identity dispute.
survey: Scan three cooperative identity repeaters along the disputed freight corridor.
TOREN: A colour on a scanner is not a warrant. Find the original signing chain.
work: Compare both duplicate keys against the independent physical seal.
HOLT: The seal's manufacturing trace proves a duplicate issue. Do not destroy the vessels carrying the evidence.
mission_action_confirmed
second: Escort the accused hauler to the independent verification berth.
HOLT: Keep both pilot and cargo safe until the receiver records the examination.
escort_arrived
choices: Publish a simultaneous revocation and safe-conduct notice
Verify the revocation receipt and militia safe-conduct acknowledgement.
TOREN: Neither duplicate becomes guilty by being the first to answer.
Reissue both keys under independent supervision
Verify two distinct replacement identities and the retired-key ledger.
HOLT: Both pilots must see the same retirement record.
clue: The seal before the key
An older layer in the physical seal contains a curved signature absent from every transponder issue record.
briefs.cover: an orbital identity workshop, two blank transponder keys with different coloured status lights beside a copper forensic seal and magnifier, distant freight beacons beyond a small window

briefs.title: The Rubble Covenant
briefs.story: A ring-mining cooperative wants to reopen a debris corridor but rival insurers classify every unclaimed rock as someone else's property. The commander maps the actual masses, attaches verified tug anchors and escorts a survey crew before choosing pooled clearance or individually bonded salvage. Safe passage depends on verified clearance and an agreed ownership charter.
survey: Measure three named debris masses and their actual drift vectors.
ORR: Ownership does not change momentum. We need both records before a tug may move anything.
work: Attach two identified tug anchors to the registered clearance bodies.
PENN: Keep anchor identity tied to the rock's conserved mass. A fragment is not a second claim.
mission_action_confirmed
second: Escort the survey tender through the proven clearance corridor.
PENN: The corridor is open only when the living survey crew receives it.
escort_arrived
choices: Pool the clearance work under the cooperative
Verify the shared mass ledger and a witnessed tug release.
ORR: All recovered material stays on the same conservation ledger.
Bond individual salvage sections
Verify section boundaries and the independent exclusion-zone test.
PENN: A private claim cannot reach across a neighbour's safe corridor.
clue: The hollow mass
One old trajectory record curves around an empty centre as though the missing mass had a boundary of its own.
briefs.cover: a practical orbital tug workbench with a bronze anchoring collar, coarse dark stone samples and a luminous measured debris corridor beyond a window, no impact or exploding station

briefs.title: A Garden in Transit
briefs.story: An orbital seed archive is moving because its lease is ending. Two destinations want the same climate collection, while the growers insist the living archive must not be divided blindly. The commander compares real receiving environments, accompanies the seed tender and obtains either a distributed custody charter or a shared quarantine berth.
survey: Scan the three receiving environmental cradles using the archive's consent token.
VEIL: A seed catalogue is not a cargo price list. Record the conditions that let it remain alive.
work: Test two isolated seed cradles with the loaned reference sampler.
ARLEN: Test capsules return to their registered owner. A copied inventory is not a new living collection.
mission_action_confirmed
second: Escort the identified seed tender to its agreed quarantine berth.
VEIL: Its custodians remain aboard until actual reception confirms their collection.
escort_arrived
choices: Create distributed seed custody
Verify two compatible climate receipts and their consented custody split.
VEIL: Split only the collection the growers agreed to share.
Establish a shared orbital archive
Verify the common quarantine lock and joint access charter.
ARLEN: A shared berth needs enforceable access for both settlements.
clue: The dormant season
The archive contains a circular season boundary that encloses no named climate or world.
briefs.cover: a quiet orbital seed-archive corridor, a sage seed case with three sealed canisters and two carefully separated climate cradles, soft green growth light and copper supports

briefs.title: The Warrant Ledger
briefs.story: Several bounty issuers have reused the same casualty evidence to obtain incompatible warrants. One convoy carries a real armed suspect and two wrongly listed witnesses. The commander audits the evidence chain, protects a neutral hearing and chooses simultaneous public correction or a protected restitution process.
survey: Scan three registered warrant evidence beacons with independent issuer signatures.
VOSS: A reward number is not evidence. A duplicate casualty cannot authorise another victim.
work: Reconcile the two conflicting victim records at the independent evidence coupler.
TOREN: The dates prove reuse. Keep the original statements and their consent restrictions intact.
mission_action_confirmed
second: Escort the consenting witness tender to the protected hearing berth.
VOSS: A living received witness is our objective. Unrelated wanted kills do not advance it.
escort_arrived
choices: Publish corrected warrants simultaneously
Verify issuer revocations and the witness safe-conduct register.
VOSS: No issuer may keep the false warrant active during publication.
Use protected restitution hearings
Verify the sealed hearing record and compensated witness custody.
TOREN: Protected testimony still needs an independent auditable receipt.
clue: The unwritten warrant
Beneath the reused evidence lies a curved jurisdiction mark naming neither a person nor an issuing world.
briefs.cover: an orbital civilian evidence office, three blank warrant tabs and a deep slate ledger core under a forensic lamp, purple tracking light reflected in glass, no guns, assassin or text

briefs.title: The Measure of Care
briefs.story: Two orbital clinics report incompatible storage readings for the same treatment. Miscalibrated refrigeration references have created an apparent shortage. The commander preserves a consented diagnostic sample, tests each cold chain and helps the clinics choose local reference standards or a jointly maintained calibration service.
survey: Read three signed cold-chain monitors without opening patient records.
DAIN: We need the equipment's history, not a stranger's diagnosis.
work: Run the sealed reference sample through the two external calibration cradles.
KEST: Keep temperature exposure and capsule identity together. A new label cannot repair a spoiled sample.
mission_action_confirmed
second: Escort the clinic service crew to the independent test berth.
DAIN: Their arrival is verified by the receiving clinic. A crate alone cannot prove care happened.
escort_arrived
choices: Keep independent clinic calibration references
Verify both reference calibrations and independent custody records.
KEST: Independence needs measured agreement, not identical software.
Establish a shared clinical calibration service
Verify the shared service limit and each clinic's stop authority.
DAIN: Either clinic must be able to stop unsafe transfers.
clue: The temperature of silence
A reference recorder shows a stable curved boundary during a period with no recorded thermal source.
briefs.cover: a civilian orbital clinic laboratory, a sealed blue-white diagnostic cold crate and independent calibration dials, calm cream work surfaces with cyan light, no patient faces or medical insignia

briefs.title: The Long Return
briefs.story: A dispersed maintenance crew can return home only if three competing carriers honour the same transfer agreement. Each carrier has a plausible but incomplete account of an earlier missed rendezvous. The commander reconstructs the physical custody chain, escorts a voluntary reunion tender and negotiates a shared handoff or direct return.
survey: Record three carrier rendezvous receipts from consenting relay crews.
SOREL: Each crew remembers a different clock. Ask who actually received people, not who filed first.
work: Test two neutral custody handoffs using the loaned receiver witness.
DAIN: These tests contain no passengers. Never make a real crew the bait for a missed rendezvous.
mission_action_confirmed
second: Escort the named reunion tender to its consented receiving berth.
SOREL: Keep the surviving crew list honest. A substitute hull does not restore someone lost.
escort_arrived
choices: Use a witnessed shared return handoff
Verify both carrier signatures and the live crew reception.
DAIN: Shared responsibility must still identify who received each person.
Give the reunion tender a direct return corridor
Verify the corridor reservation and home-berth arrival authority.
SOREL: A direct journey is safe only if its last berth is real.
clue: The passenger never booked
The oldest rendezvous record reserves a curved empty space with no passenger, mass or destination.
briefs.cover: an empty orbital crew-transfer lounge, cream seating, a red-edged custody recorder and three calm rendezvous lights through a window, humane quiet atmosphere without people

briefs.title: The Unfinished Map
briefs.story: A dead surveyor's archive is being sold as a complete safe-navigation map, although its final measurements were never made. The commander recovers authorised copies from ordinary visible receivers, measures the disputed gaps and obtains either a clearly bounded public atlas or a witnessed research-only archive.
survey: Compare three independently dated boundary records at the survey relays.
ORR: An honest blank is safer than an invented coordinate.
work: Measure two uncharted orbital boundary points using the loaned survey register.
VALE: Record uncertainty with the reading. Do not turn an estimate into a historical fact.
mission_action_confirmed
second: Escort the consenting archive custodian to the publication berth.
VALE: The custodian brings the original rights register. A stolen copy cannot grant consent.
escort_arrived
choices: Publish a bounded atlas with explicit gaps
Verify the uncertainty layer and public-use consent record.
ORR: The blank areas must survive publication.
Preserve a witnessed research archive
Verify the restricted archive receipt and a public hazard notice.
VALE: Restricted research cannot keep a known flight hazard secret.
clue: The margin beyond the map
The archive's untouched margin carries an inward arc outside every surveyed coordinate frame.
briefs.cover: an original orbital cartography desk, dark blank atlas plates and a copper survey register, disconnected cyan boundary arcs above a sparse star field, no familiar galactic map

briefs.title: The Blue Reservoir
briefs.story: An orbital water commons is losing dissolved oxygen while every intake remains clean. A new circulation pump has trapped part of the living filter behind a one-way lease boundary. The commander measures actual flow, opens consented bypasses and chooses distributed filter cradles or a jointly governed reservoir.
survey: Scan three oxygen and flow monitors on the external reservoir manifold.
LERR: Clean intake water says nothing about what the circulation loop keeps from returning.
work: Open two measured bypass locks without releasing the living filter.
VEIL: The colony remains contained. A destroyed tank is neither a repair nor a rescued organism.
mission_action_confirmed
second: Escort the water-commons inspection tender to the safe laboratory berth.
LERR: Its operators must observe the actual flow before accepting it.
escort_arrived
choices: Distribute the living filter among independent cradles
Verify both containment receipts and balanced flow tests.
VEIL: Divide only a viable culture, with each receiver's consent.
Create a jointly supervised reservoir
Verify common circulation limits and independent shutdown authority.
LERR: Shared water needs a physical limit as well as a charter.
clue: The dry current
The oldest flow recorder traces an inward curve through a channel that contains no water.
briefs.cover: an orbital water-commons control bay, blue translucent circulation loops around a contained pale green living filter, original ivory and teal machinery, no sea creature or submerged city

briefs.title: Mutual Shelter
briefs.story: A repair mutual has insured more emergency shelter than its docks can physically provide. A legal salvage claim on a disabled hauler exposes the shortfall. The commander measures real capacity, protects the hauler's crew and helps members choose a pooled reserve or independently bonded shelter.
survey: Scan three emergency-dock capacity registers and their physical berth limits.
TOREN: A promise of shelter is useful only if a ship can actually fit.
work: Reserve two real emergency berths against the independently measured capacity ledger.
ARLEN: Reserve the space once. Selling a second receipt does not create another berth.
mission_action_confirmed
second: Escort the disabled cooperative hauler to its verified repair berth.
ARLEN: Its crew keeps its title while the repairs and hearing take place.
escort_arrived
choices: Pool member-funded emergency capacity
Verify the real reserve ledger and member withdrawal limits.
TOREN: Publish what is covered before accepting anyone's contribution.
Bond independent shelter obligations
Verify each provider's berth bond and an actual receiving drill.
ARLEN: A bond needs a berth behind it, not another bond.
clue: The ownerless reserve
An early shelter ledger reserves an inward-shaped volume that has never been assigned a hull or creditor.
briefs.cover: an orbital cooperative repair office, a bronze emergency-capacity ledger and two blank berth tokens, warm cream lighting and orderly drydock gantries in the distance

briefs.title: The Listening Frontier
briefs.story: Human survey bursts are compressing a Larvaal migration channel into a narrow dangerous crossing. Both sides report collisions as attacks. The commander measures independent traces, establishes protected listening intervals and escorts a neutral witness before choosing distributed quiet windows or a shared migration relay.
survey: Record three consenting human and Larvaal boundary listeners.
HOLT: Keep weapon signatures apart from survey bursts. A crowded channel does not prove an invasion.
work: Calibrate two external quiet-window emitters using the reference listener.
VALE: The window must leave room for a reply. Broadcasting louder is not listening.
mission_action_confirmed
second: Escort the neutral listening tender to its protected receiving berth.
HOLT: Protect the witness rather than farming incidental combat kills.
escort_arrived
choices: Publish independent quiet windows
Verify human schedule withdrawal and Larvaal acknowledgement.
VALE: Each side needs a measured interval it can trust.
Establish a jointly witnessed migration relay
Verify relay limits and both independent reply receipts.
HOLT: No single operator may close the other's return path.
clue: The voice outside the channel
A quiet-window listener receives an inward-curved phase trace from outside both recognised transmission bands.
briefs.cover: a silent orbital listening observatory, smooth jade crescent instruments and two separate human cyan and alien gold signal paths leaving a quiet gap, no warships or battle

briefs.title: An Assembly of Orbits
briefs.story: A cluster of orbital homes must share a single transfer corridor during a maintenance season. Old voting records count property shares but omit the crews who keep the corridor open. The commander verifies real occupancy and operating work, escorts delegates and establishes either rotating worker stewardship or publicly bounded berth representation.
survey: Compare three consented occupancy and corridor-work registers.
VOSS: A share certificate cannot stand in for the people on the next shift.
work: Run two independent corridor-capacity tests with the loaned assembly console.
DAIN: Show every group the same limits before asking it to choose.
mission_action_confirmed
second: Escort the consenting delegate tender to the neutral assembly berth.
VOSS: The hearing requires received delegates, not an empty passenger manifest.
escort_arrived
choices: Rotate corridor stewardship among working crews
Verify the rota and each crew's stop authority.
DAIN: Rotation needs a safe handover, not a race to the controls.
Use bounded public berth representation
Verify the published representation register and capacity cap.
VOSS: No vote can create more corridor than the measured envelope.
clue: The absent seat
The oldest assembly diagram encloses an empty central seat with a curved boundary absent from all membership lists.
briefs.cover: an empty neutral orbital assembly chamber, circular civilian work consoles around a deliberately unoccupied centre, cream and maroon fittings, no throne, flags or insignia

briefs.title: Under Tow
briefs.story: An emergency transport network has standardised its forms but not the physical coupling limits of its vessels. A stranded work tender cannot accept the rescue tug sent for it. The commander measures real hull interfaces, recovers an independent coupler and verifies either interoperable local rescue pairs or a shared specialist tender. Crew identity, actual docking and return custody determine success.
survey: Scan three rescue-interface collars and their independent load limits.
PENN: Matching form numbers do not make these collars fit.
work: Test two compatible couplings with the loaned service reference.
DAIN: Test against empty cradles first. People are not calibration weights.
mission_action_confirmed
second: Escort the identified rescued work tender to an actually compatible berth.
PENN: It stays a real vessel with a living crew until reception records the handoff.
escort_arrived
choices: Accredit interoperable local rescue pairs
Verify two tested coupling pairs and their crew reception drill.
PENN: A local promise must identify the tug that can keep it.
Establish a shared specialist rescue tender
Verify specialist dispatch limits and the receiving-station agreement.
DAIN: Shared rescue capacity cannot be sold twice.
clue: The coupling without a vessel
An old interface calibration defines a curved inward contact surface with no compatible hull in its register.
briefs.cover: an original orbital rescue workshop, a slate and copper load coupler between two visibly different empty interface cradles, amber safety lights, no branded rescue ship

briefs.title: The Memory Atlas
briefs.story: A navigation publisher has combined voluntary travel diaries with instrument surveys and now presents memories as exact route measurements. The commander revisits three disputed orbital landmarks, separates consented testimony from physical data and chooses an annotated public atlas or a custodian-held memory archive.
survey: Record three orbital landmarks independently of the travel diaries.
ORR: A beautiful memory is not a measured approach vector.
work: Compare two landmark instruments against the loaned reference watcher.
VALE: Keep consent attached to testimony and uncertainty attached to measurements.
mission_action_confirmed
second: Escort the consenting diary custodian to the archive receiving berth.
VALE: The custodian decides which memories become public.
escort_arrived
choices: Publish a separated evidence-and-memory atlas
Verify independent measurement labels and each contributor's consent.
ORR: Let readers see where testimony ends and the instrument begins.
Keep the diaries with their custodians
Verify restricted custody and publish only measured hazard corrections.
VALE: Privacy does not require keeping an unsafe chart in circulation.
clue: The place nobody remembers
Three unrelated diaries contain the same inward curve around a place none of their authors visited.
briefs.cover: an orbital archive desk, blank translucent memory plates beside a navy survey watcher and sparse cyan landmark markers, warm copper lamps, no recognisable source star chart

briefs.title: A Fleet of Neighbours
briefs.story: Three settlements offer civilian protection ships after pirates close a relief corridor. Their hulls and fuel are finite, and every commander wants the same escort window. The player audits actual commitments, repairs a relief lane and escorts a dispatch tender before choosing a rotating protection rota or locally retained reserve pairs. Aid comes from the ships that actually arrive.
survey: Verify three real relief-escort manifests and their available fuel.
ARLEN: A promised hull cannot protect a corridor it has not reached.
work: Repair two external relief-lane relays with the loaned dispatch beacon.
VOSS: Keep the repair separate from the defence. A pirate kill cannot calibrate a relay.
mission_action_confirmed
second: Escort the registered civilian dispatch tender to relief reception.
ARLEN: Record arrivals and losses honestly. Do not recreate a destroyed helper from its promise.
escort_arrived
choices: Rotate arrived protection ships across settlements
Verify the arrived-hull rota and each crew's consented duty limit.
VOSS: Duty changes only when the actual replacement arrives.
Retain local reserve pairs with mutual callouts
Verify both local reserves and a real cross-settlement callout.
ARLEN: A reserve is a living ship, not an accounting entry.
clue: The formation with no centre
An early dispatch diagram curves around an empty central formation slot with no assigned vessel.
briefs.cover: a civilian orbital dispatch bay, three distinct unmarked escort tokens and a copper route beacon, a distant relief lane of amber lights, no military emblems or combat

briefs.title: Uncounted Names
briefs.story: A dock automation system records a group of displaced workers as transferable industrial property because their first manifests used equipment-only forms. The commander obtains consented identities, establishes safe reception and helps the workers choose a private custody correction or a public register repair.
survey: Compare three consented identity receipts without publishing private names.
DAIN: Ask the people concerned how their records should be used.
work: Correct two external receiving permissions under witnessed consent.
TOREN: The old manifest remains evidence, not an authority to transfer a person.
mission_action_confirmed
second: Escort the consenting worker tender to its chosen safe receiving berth.
DAIN: Only living consenting arrivals count. Cargo canisters cannot represent people.
escort_arrived
choices: Repair individual records under protected custody
Verify each consented correction and independent reception authority.
TOREN: A correction must not erase the evidence of what went wrong.
Publish a systematic register repair
Verify anonymised audit results and the permanent form correction.
DAIN: Publish the fault without publishing the people who suffered it.
clue: The unnamed entry
The oldest register has an inward-curved entry naming no person, cargo or owner.
briefs.cover: a calm orbital reception office, cream custody register and blank private identity tabs under a soft lamp, an open receiving corridor in the distance, no captive people or branded symbols

briefs.title: The Honest Circuit
briefs.story: A new flight certification circuit rewards apparent speed without accounting for unsafe close passes or offloaded fuel. The commander independently measures its beacons, completes a real receiving test and chooses an efficiency standard or a safety-margin standard. The player completes the circuit with their current commander and ship.
survey: Scan three circuit beacons and compare their independent timebases.
VENN: A fast time means little if the clock and the route disagree.
work: Complete two published corridor tests with the reference timing standard.
RENN: Every limit is visible before the run. Pausing preserves the simulation clock.
mission_action_confirmed
second: Escort the consenting calibration tender through the same certified corridor.
VENN: The standard must work for a working tender as well as a fast player ship.
escort_arrived
choices: Certify measured route efficiency
Verify fuel accounting and actual receiving time.
RENN: Efficiency includes the fuel actually used, not a removed manifest.
Certify a minimum safety margin
Verify the closest-pass envelope and emergency abort test.
VENN: A safe abort is a valid measured result, not a punishment.
clue: The tick outside the circuit
A reference timebase records a curved phase mark between two valid circuit ticks.
briefs.cover: an orbital flight-calibration desk with a circular silver timing instrument, three independent cyan route arcs and an amber safety envelope through dark glass, no race branding

briefs.title: Small Lights
briefs.story: A cluster of modest utility failures is ignored because each falls below an insurer's dispatch threshold. Together they isolate an orbital neighbourhood. The commander measures the combined fault, repairs actual receiving modules and escorts a maintenance crew before establishing pooled local callouts or independently funded service reserves.
survey: Read three neighbourhood utility faults and their actual shared dependencies.
SENN: Small failures become large when every office treats them as someone else's.
work: Restore two external service modules with the loaned utility lantern.
LERR: Confirm the actual load before clearing a fault from the board.
mission_action_confirmed
second: Escort the consenting maintenance tender to the neighbourhood berth.
SENN: The crew has to reach its work, not merely accept a dispatch.
escort_arrived
choices: Pool local callouts across utilities
Verify a shared capacity ledger and a real cross-utility response.
LERR: Shared work needs spare capacity behind it.
Keep independently funded service reserves
Verify two stocked reserves and their receiving drill.
SENN: Count the parts on the shelf, not the promises on the form.
clue: The light before the fault
An old utility lantern records an inward pulse before any of the neighbourhood's equipment was installed.
briefs.cover: an original orbital neighbourhood utility alcove, three small amber service lanterns around a slate maintenance programmer, warm lights on a dark planet beyond, hopeful modest scale

briefs.title: The Passenger's Horizon
briefs.story: A passenger cooperative sells a scenic orbital journey that excludes travellers whose cabin needs do not match its standard form. The commander tests real access and safe viewing positions, escorts a volunteer assessment tender and helps the travellers establish either adaptable shared cabins or individually guaranteed journey slots. Consent and actual fitted capacity determine the journey plan.
survey: Scan three orbital viewing and receiving sites against the travellers' consented access needs.
SOREL: A fine horizon is useless if a passenger cannot safely reach it.
work: Test two external boarding and viewing interfaces with the loaned access console.
DAIN: Use an empty test cradle first. People do not have to prove that an unsafe fitting hurts.
mission_action_confirmed
second: Escort the consenting assessment tender to its independently verified berth.
SOREL: Their actual reception is the evidence; a passenger count alone is not.
escort_arrived
choices: Provide adaptable shared journey cabins
Verify compatible fittings and each traveller's independent consent.
DAIN: Shared access cannot erase an individual's needs.
Guarantee individual accessible journey slots
Verify reserved capacity and the safe receiving itinerary.
SOREL: A reservation includes every receiving point, not just departure.
clue: The horizon without a world
A viewing reference encloses an inward-curved horizon that belongs to none of the surveyed planets.
briefs.cover: an empty accessible civilian orbital passenger lounge, cream and teal interface console, broad unobstructed viewing glass over a blue planet, calm inclusive working environment

briefs.title: The Kind Distance
briefs.story: Two separated households want to restore contact but disagree about who may disclose their new locations. A relay broker offers to solve the problem by publishing both addresses. The commander measures private reply paths, verifies voluntary custody and helps the households choose an anonymous shared relay or individually revocable invitations. The households retain the right to decline a meeting.
survey: Test three private reply relays without exposing either household's address.
SOL: A reply means someone chose to answer. Silence is not consent.
work: Verify two anonymous invitation paths with the loaned passive receiver.
DAIN: The message may cross the boundary. The address must not follow without permission.
mission_action_confirmed
second: Escort the consenting relay custodian to the independent privacy hearing berth.
SOL: The custodian can confirm the rules without carrying either household.
escort_arrived
choices: Use an anonymous shared reply relay
Verify independent revocation and a consented reply receipt.
DAIN: Either household may close its path without closing the other's.
Issue individually revocable invitations

briefs.title: Cold Reserve
briefs.story: A decommissioned defence reserve is still paying for autonomous cargo movements under expired authority. Its unmanned equipment is still executing the expired dispatch orders. The commander reconciles finite stores, disconnects real dispatch couplers and escorts an inspection crew before choosing a civilian reserve conversion or verified dismantling.
survey: Scan three reserve store ledgers and their actual physical inventories.
PELL: Count what is here before anyone orders it somewhere else.
work: Isolate two named external dispatch couplers from expired work authority.
VOSS: Unmanned couplers are the target. Random military hulls and stations are not substitutes.
mission_action_confirmed
second: Escort the independent inspection tender to the safe reserve berth.
PELL: The inspectors must see the emptied dispatch path themselves.
escort_arrived
choices: Convert the finite reserve to civilian emergency use
Verify capped civilian authority and actual received stock.
VOSS: No old order may survive behind the new label.
Dismantle and reclaim the reserve
Verify dispatch isolation and conserved material reception.
PELL: Scenery disappearing is not material arriving.
clue: The unused order

briefs.cover: a cold orbital storage hall, finite dark reserve canisters with copper caps beside an isolated dispatch coupler, amber manual lock lights, no weapons or military insignia

briefs.title: The Magnetic Orchard
briefs.story: A slowly growing Larvaal structure bends charged dust into living magnetic fronds. Human survey tethers disturb its growth, while some operators mistake the fronds for collectible weapons. The commander measures the field without taking living parts, removes two consented tethers and chooses protected independent boundaries or a jointly observed growth reserve.
survey: Observe three safe magnetic field boundaries without extracting living material.
VALE: A living structure is not a rack of salvage waiting for a buyer.
work: Release two identified human tethers using the isolated field reference.
KEST: Keep the removed tether mass in custody. Cutting a frond is not removing our equipment.
mission_action_confirmed
second: Escort the neutral observation tender to the protected receiving cradle.
VALE: Bring the observers through the measured gap rather than forcing a new one.
escort_arrived
choices: Protect independent human and Larvaal growth boundaries
Verify both exclusion envelopes and their reply receipts.
KEST: Each boundary needs room to change without touching the other.
Establish a jointly observed growth reserve
Verify the consented reserve and independent monitoring limits.
VALE: Observation does not grant ownership.
clue: The root without a stem

briefs.cover: an original orbital observation room overlooking smooth jade crescent growth instruments and fine gold charged-dust fronds in space, scientific rather than monstrous, no ships or blades

briefs.title: Open Measure
briefs.story: Three independent workshops cannot exchange replacement parts because their calibration certificates use incompatible reference loads. A supplier profits by treating each disagreement as a new proprietary component. The commander measures actual tolerances, tests shared reference fittings and escorts a neutral technician before choosing public measurement standards or a witnessed interoperable service.
survey: Compare three workshop reference loads against the actual external test fittings.
LERR: A certificate should describe a fit, not manufacture a monopoly.
work: Test two independently made parts with the loaned tolerance programmer.
KEST: Record the physical tolerances before looking at the supplier's label.
mission_action_confirmed
second: Escort the independent calibration tender to the common test berth.
LERR: Its technician brings a separate instrument and a separate signing key.
escort_arrived
choices: Publish an open physical measurement standard

KEST: A standard works when someone else can reproduce it.
Establish a witnessed interoperable calibration service
Verify reciprocal service limits and independent rejection rights.
LERR: Every workshop must be able to refuse an unsafe result.
clue: The reference without a load

briefs.title: The Shared Pulse
briefs.story: A Larvaal maintenance organ and a human beacon exchange incompatible acknowledgement pulses. Each automatically repeats faster when it receives the other's reply, creating a hazardous feedback loop. The commander establishes independent listening references, restores a consenting repair organ and verifies either separated timing windows or a shared bounded handshake.
survey: Measure three independent points around the feedback loop without rebroadcasting it.

work: Install the consented repair reference at two external handshake couplers.
VALE: The organ remains with its custodian. A repair is not a specimen theft.

briefs.title: The Witness Window

briefs.title: Public Record
briefs.story: An orbital news service wants to report a dangerous cargo-routing fault, but its sponsor owns the only accepted recording instrument.
